objective: Add a provider-neutral agent-aware fleet-intent control plane that complements Kubernetes and GPU scheduling ecosystems with durable identity, lineage, topology/resource policy, deterministic gang placement, stale-generation fencing, fail-closed authorization, and replacement-node recovery.

verified_ecosystem_capabilities: Kubernetes DRA resource claims, device classes, device filtering, sharing, device status, and health monitoring
Kueue hierarchical topology-aware scheduling using node labels and capacity calculation
Kueue workload queues, fair sharing, preemption, all-or-nothing/gang concepts, autoscaler support, and MultiKueue concepts
research.design_conclusion: Kubernetes and GPU operators remain stronger for live cluster lifecycle, declarative reconciliation, device drivers, autoscaling, service discovery, and physical accelerator operations. FAISAL adds a trusted agent/objective governance layer above them rather than replacing them.

features: agent, tenant, objective, policy-generation, and lineage binding
CPU, memory, accelerator, capability, and health eligibility checks
deterministic topology/resource score and stable node-ID tie-breaking
gang placement across distinct eligible nodes
node generation fencing and stale placement rejection
node failure detection and replacement-node recovery

benchmark.scope: local userspace policy fixture, not Kubernetes or physical GPU qualification

comparison.scope: FAISAL agent-aware placement/governance fixture versus Kubernetes DRA/Kueue/GPU-fleet operations
comparison.faisal_advantage: explicit objective/agent lineage, authority, stale-generation fencing, placement evidence, and deterministic replacement recovery at the control-plane boundary
comparison.ecosystem_advantage: live Kubernetes reconciliation, DRA/device drivers, node and pod lifecycle, service discovery, autoscaling, topology APIs, queueing, and physical GPU isolation/health
required_before_fleet_superiority_claim: actual GPU/NPU devices and vendor driver

boundary.note: M225 is a provider-neutral trusted fleet-intent and recovery policy layer. It does not replace Kubernetes, DRA, Kueue, GPU Operator, device drivers, kubelet, autoscalers, or physical hardware, and it does not establish production fleet readiness.
